title: Meet the founders of Ampersand: Ayan Barua and Lauren Long
gist: Bessemer is leading Ampersand's $15M Series A, arguing that per-customer integration work (custom Salesforce objects, fields, permissions) is the hidden implementation tax protecting legacy systems of record, and that agents make it urgent because they cannot absorb customer configuration like a solutions engineer. Ampersand's pitch is declare-once, version-controlled integrations that resolve per-tenant schemas at runtime, with a claimed 90% PoC-to-paid conversion.

insights.claim: The deepest moat protecting legacy systems of record is the cost of implementing and customizing them for every enterprise; Bessemer's investment thesis is that Ampersand dissolves that moat by turning the per-customer integration project into version-controlled code.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: If per-tenant customization stops being a switching-cost barrier for agent-native entrants, incumbent CRM/ERP lock-in weakens; watch for agent-layer vendors displacing seat-based incumbents.
insights.quote: the deepest moat protecting legacy systems of record is the cost of implementing and customizing them for every enterprise
insights.locator: In our Roadmap: AI systems of action

insights.claim: For enterprise software vendors, the hard part of integration is not connecting to Salesforce but connecting to each customer's distinct Salesforce, with different objects, fields and permissions, and the same repeats across HubSpot, Dynamics, Oracle, SAP and every vertical system.
insights.speaker: Ayan Barua and Lauren Long
insights.so_what: Integration cost scales with customer count rather than product, a hidden margin and roadmap drag for application vendors.
insights.quote: connecting to Salesforce isn't the hard part. Connecting to each customer's Salesforce is.

insights.claim: Before tooling like this, engineering time went to onboarding each customer, fixing integrations that broke quietly, and pulling senior engineers off the core product to do both, so integration timelines bent product roadmaps and stalled deals.
insights.speaker: Ayan Barua and Lauren Long
insights.so_what: Vendors with heavy enterprise onboarding likely have understated services-like cost in their gross margin; integration automation is a margin and sales-velocity lever.
insights.locator: Their time went to three places

themes.theme: Agents raise the stakes on integration

insights.claim: Agents make the per-customer integration problem more urgent because an agent cannot learn a customer's configuration on the job the way a product or solutions engineer can; the founders say it is the same old problem but 100x more complex at agentic scale.
insights.speaker: Ayan Barua and Lauren Long
insights.so_what: Agent deployments into enterprises will be gated by data-access plumbing rather than model quality, favoring infrastructure that makes each tenant legible to software.
insights.quote: an agent can't learn a customer's configuration on the job the way a product engineer or a solution engineer can
insights.locator: So this deep integration problem was true long before agents

insights.claim: Agents run continuously, so a changed schema or expired credential can silently break production; the founders position reliability on 'day 200' (schema-drift audits, automatic credential management, real-time alerts) as the differentiator, claiming resolution time falls from days to seconds.
insights.speaker: Ayan Barua and Lauren Long
insights.so_what: Operational durability, not demo-stage connectivity, is where integration vendors will win or lose; a vendor-claimed figure, not independently verified.
insights.quote: we built for day 200, not only day one

insights.claim: The founders' long-run ambition is to move from deep CRM and ERP integration to broader enterprise software and eventually a shared interoperability layer any agent can use, on the framing that enterprise systems were built for people, hardened for engineers, and now must be made legible to agents.
insights.speaker: Ayan Barua and Lauren Long
insights.so_what: An agent interoperability layer is a potential chokepoint with platform-like economics; also a competitive risk to the incumbents' own agent strategies.
insights.quote: Enterprise systems were built for people, then hardened for engineers. Our job is to make them legible to agents.
insights.locator: We're starting with deep CRM and ERP integration

insights.claim: Ampersand rejects lowest-common-denominator unified schemas: it reads and writes in each system's native structure because custom objects and fields are where the business actually lives, which is why flattened tools work in demos but break on real enterprise accounts.
insights.speaker: Ayan Barua and Lauren Long
insights.so_what: Implicitly a challenge to unified-API competitors; native-schema depth is the claimed durable differentiator for agent use cases that must know which field marks a deal as qualified.
insights.quote: That works in a demo and breaks on a real enterprise account, because the custom objects and fields are where the business actually lives.

insights.claim: Integrations are declared once in version-controlled code using five primitives (read, write, subscribe, search, proxy), live in the customer's own repository and ship through normal review and deployment, while the end customer's admin does field mapping in the vendor's onboarding flow.
insights.speaker: Ayan Barua and Lauren Long
insights.so_what: Shifts the work from vendor engineers and forward-deployed staff to the customer's admin and to code, reducing the product-to-FDE gap and ongoing babysitting.
insights.locator: With Ampersand, a developer declares the integration once

insights.claim: Keeping integration logic as inspectable code in the customer's own repository, rather than inside a black box, is a deliberate trust and control bet, with every tenant fully isolated so the same integration scales from one enterprise customer to hundreds.
insights.speaker: Ayan Barua and Lauren Long
insights.so_what: Developer control and tenant isolation address enterprise security and procurement objections that block opaque integration platforms.

insights.claim: Enterprise system customization will not be standardized away: it encodes how a company sells, bills and runs, so the field marking a qualified deal differs at every company, and scaling therefore requires treating variation as the default rather than waiting for simplification.
insights.speaker: Ayan Barua and Lauren Long
insights.so_what: Bets against a convergence-to-standard-schema future; implies enduring demand for translation layers and sustained moat value in customized systems of record.
insights.quote: Customization isn't technical debt. It's how a company encodes the way it sells, bills, and runs.
insights.locator: It's permanent, and it should be

insights.claim: The stated goal is to make the question of how long it will take to connect a closed enterprise deal to the customer's CRM, ERP, payroll and communication systems disappear, so the roadmap stops bending around integration timelines and best engineers return to the core product.
insights.speaker: Ayan Barua and Lauren Long
insights.so_what: Faster time-to-value on enterprise deals would shorten sales cycles for application vendors that adopt this kind of layer.

insights.claim: Bessemer is leading Ampersand's $15M Series A, and the company reports that teams who complete a proof of concept become paying customers 90% of the time.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: A 90% PoC conversion is a strong but self-reported figure with no stated sample size; it suggests pain acuity but should be discounted for selection effects.
insights.quote: Teams that finish a proof of concept with us become paying customers 90% of the time.
insights.locator: You can see it in conversion

insights.claim: Many Ampersand customers arrive after a failed integration deployment elsewhere, and the founders validated the problem through conversations with more than 100 application-layer companies that must deal with customers' systems of record.
insights.speaker: Ayan Barua and Lauren Long
insights.so_what: Displacement of failed incumbents suggests the market is already paying for integration solutions and is dissatisfied with existing options.
insights.quote: we spoke with more than 100 companies in various domains on the application layer that have to deal with customers’ systems of record
